questions.q: A section of code in which a process accesses shared data, and which must not be executed concurrently by another process, is called the ______.
questions.e: The critical section is the code that touches shared resources. A race condition is the faulty outcome when it is not protected.

questions.q: A semaphore that can take only the values 0 and 1 is called a ______ semaphore.
questions.e: A binary semaphore has values 0 and 1 and is used for mutual exclusion. A counting semaphore can take any non-negative integer value.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a necessary condition for deadlock?
questions.e: The four necessary conditions are mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no pre-emption and circular wait. Pre-emption of resources would help break a deadlock.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about paging.
I. Paging eliminates external fragmentation.
II. The last page of a process may waste some space, causing internal fragmentation.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are true. Any free frame can hold any page, so there is no external fragmentation. The partly filled last page causes internal fragmentation.

questions.q: In demand paging, a page is brought into main memory ______.
o: before the process starts, for all its pages
only when it is referenced and found absent (page fault)
only when the disk is idle
questions.e: Demand paging loads a page lazily on a page fault. Loading all pages in advance would be ordinary (non-virtual) loading.

questions.q: When a system spends more time paging than executing useful work, it is said to be ______.
questions.e: Thrashing occurs when processes do not have enough frames, so page faults dominate and CPU utilisation falls.

questions.q:
Regarding page replacement, consider the following statements.
I. FIFO page replacement can show Belady's anomaly.
II. LRU page replacement can show Belady's anomaly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only I is correct. With FIFO, giving more frames can sometimes cause more page faults. LRU is a stack algorithm and never shows the anomaly.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the optimal page replacement algorithm.
I. It replaces the page that was used least recently in the past.
II. It replaces the page that will not be used for the longest period in the future.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only II is correct. Optimal looks ahead and evicts the page whose next use is farthest away. Replacing the least recently used page is the LRU policy.

questions.q: SPOOL stands for ______.
questions.e: Spooling overlaps the slow I/O of one job with the computation of others by buffering data on disk, as with a print queue.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a disk scheduling algorithm?
questions.e: Banker's algorithm is used for deadlock avoidance. SCAN, C-SCAN and SSTF decide the order in which disk requests are served.

questions.q: Which technique uses an area of main memory to hold data temporarily while it is transferred between two devices of different speeds?
questions.e: A buffer is a region of memory used to smooth speed differences between producer and consumer. Spooling, by contrast, uses disk.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT true of contiguous file allocation?
o: The file size must be known or estimated in advance
It supports fast direct access to blocks
A file can grow easily without being moved
questions.e: Contiguous allocation needs one run of adjacent blocks, so a file cannot easily grow in place and may need to be moved. Linked and indexed allocation avoid this.

questions.q: A system has a 32-bit logical address, 4 KB pages and 4-byte page-table entries, with single-level paging. The size of the page table is ______.
questions.e: Offset is 12 bits, so there are 2²⁰ pages. The table size is 2²⁰ × 4 B = 4 MB.

questions.q: A machine has 64 MB of physical memory and a page size of 4 KB. The number of frames is ______.
questions.e: 64 MB / 4 KB = 2²⁶ / 2¹² = 2¹⁴ = 16384 frames.

questions.q: A counting semaphore is initialised to 2. Five wait (P) operations and then one signal (V) operation are performed by different processes. Taking a negative value to mean the number of blocked processes, the final value is ______.
questions.e: Value = 2 − 5 + 1 = −2. Two P operations pass, three block, and the V releases one of those, leaving two blocked.

questions.q: In the bounded-buffer (producer-consumer) problem with N slots, the semaphores mutex, empty and full are initialised, in that order, to ______.
questions.e: Mutex starts at 1 for exclusive access, empty counts free slots (N) and full counts filled slots (0).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about a resource-allocation graph.
I. If every resource type has a single instance, a cycle implies a deadlock.
II. If resource types have multiple instances, a cycle only indicates a possible deadlock.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Both are true. With single instances a cycle is necessary and sufficient for deadlock. With multiple instances the cycle is necessary but not sufficient.

questions.q: A process with 3 frames references the pages 1, 3, 5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 3, 5 in this order. The number of page faults under optimal replacement is ______.
questions.e: Faults occur for 1, 3, 5, 2, 4 and the final 5; the references 1, 3, 1 and 3 hit. Total 6 faults.

questions.q: For the reference string 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, FIFO replacement with 4 frames produces ______ page faults.
questions.e: With 3 frames FIFO gives 9 faults, but with 4 frames it gives 10, which is Belady's anomaly.

questions.q: A disk head is at cylinder 50 and the request queue is 82, 170, 43, 140, 24, 16, 190. Using SSTF, the total head movement is ______ cylinders.

Consider the following statements about monitors.
I. Several processes may be active inside a monitor at the same time.
II. A monitor guarantees that deadlock can never occur.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Neither is correct. A monitor allows only one process to be active inside it at any moment, giving mutual exclusion. It does not prevent deadlock by itself.

questions.q: Four processes each need a maximum of 3 units of a single resource type. The minimum number of units that guarantees the system can never deadlock is ______.
questions.e: The worst case gives each process 2 units (4 × 2 = 8) and everyone waits. One extra unit, 4 × (3 − 1) + 1 = 9, lets some process finish.

questions.q: Processes P1, P2 and P3 arrive at time 0 with CPU bursts of 10, 4 and 6 ms and are scheduled by round robin with a time quantum of 4 ms in that order. P3 completes at time ______.
questions.e: Timeline: P1 0-4, P2 4-8 (done), P3 8-12, P1 12-16, P3 16-18 (done), P1 18-20. So P3 completes at 18 ms.

questions.q: Memory access takes 200 ns, a page-fault service takes 8 ms, and the page-fault rate is 1 in 1000 references. The effective access time is approximately ______.
questions.e: EAT = 0.999 × 200 + 0.001 × 8,000,000 = 199.8 + 8000 = 8199.8 ns. Page faults slow memory access by about 40 times.

questions.q: A disk has cylinders 0 to 199. The head is at 53 moving towards cylinder 0, and the queue is 98, 183, 37, 122, 14, 124, 65, 67. Using SCAN (the head goes to cylinder 0, then reverses and serves the rest up to the last request), the total head movement is ______ cylinders.
questions.e: Head goes 53→0 (53), then 0→183 (183), the farthest request. Total 53 + 183 = 236. The value 208 is the LOOK result, which stops at 14.
